I will still do wheat and maize on all 10.1 mu, same as before. I have done this rotation many years, and I do not like changing too much at my age. My land has well water, so I will lean a little heavier on fertilizer rather than gamble on a thin crop. For wheat, I will keep improved seed, give enough nitrogen, and make sure the key waterings are not missed. Around here, if wheat is short of fertilizer or misses water at jointing, the ears do not fill well, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like many people nearby do, because I have seen it give a steadier harvest. I will put more fertilizer on maize too, but not wildly, because I still have to leave money for spray and field work. On 10.1 mu, I can manage it with family labor and a little hired help if the busy time comes together. I will mostly follow last year’s way, then push yield a little with timely water, enough base fertilizer, and topdressing when the crop is really taking off.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all 10.1 mu and mostly follow what worked last year, because changing too much is risky and every yuan matters. Since I have well irrigation, I will support the crop with steady water and a little heavier fertilizer so I do not lose yield from weak growth. For wheat I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen and the main waterings, and spray three times to hold disease and insects down. For maize I will use hybrid seed, feed it well during fast growth, irrigate twice if rain is not enough, and spray twice.
